text:
ivy: monitoring alert — SCIM deprov error rate jumped to ~16% at 15:22 UTC, lots of 403s and a few orphaned svcaccs. anyone touch RBAC or service principals?
ron: I merged a small mapping rename at 15:10 that changed the TF role the provisioner uses (arn:aws:iam::888999000111:role/scim-provisioner -> arn:aws:iam::888999000111:role/scim-provisioner-renamed). Didn’t touch key policies.
kate: grabbing logs — seeing repeated: 
```
2026-03-11T15:21:58Z ERROR scim-deprov decrypt extid err="AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:888999000111:key/1a2b3c4d"
```
kate: KMS denies look like the new principal isn't in the key policy. when that happens decrypt fails and items get queued -> orphaned accounts.
security-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3950 "SCIM deprov KMS AccessDenied after role rename" — paging eng-platform
ron: yikes, i forgot the key policy step. is there any caching we need to clear after the policy change?
tori: update key policy first (include both old and new ARNs), then restart scim-provisioner pods to drop cached KMS contexts. keep the old ARN for a 48h grace window.
ron: applying policy now and will verify with aws kms get-key-policy.
ops-bot: key policy patched at 2026-03-11T15:25:12Z (kp-change: kp-3950) — AllowScimProvisioner now includes both ARNs
ops-bot: kubectl -n idp rollout restart deployment/scim-provisioner — rolling restart started
kate: post-restart logs: 
```
2026-03-11T15:27:40Z INFO scim-deprov decrypt succeeded item=svcacc-5
2026-03-11T15:27:42Z INFO scim-deprov deprovision completed user=svcacc-5
```
ivy: running a backfill for 15:00-15:25 window now, watching error rates. initial batch zero failures.
ivy: follow-ups: 1) ron — add KMS key policy step to RBAC rename runbook; 2) eng-platform — add CI lint to flag principal ARN diffs vs key policies; 3) eng-security — improve correlation ids between SCIM and KMS logs; 4) SRE — add temporary alert for KMS AccessDenied spike from scim-provisioner.
security-bot: incident INC-2026-3950 resolved -> root cause: role rename not added to KMS key policy; remediation: updated key policy, restarted provisioner, backfilled missed deprovisions. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
